title: Allocation of Foodgrains under PM-POSHAN
body_text:
Education is part of the Concurrent List of the Constitution of India and most of the Government Schools and School Boards are under the administration of the State Government and Union Territory (UT) Administrations. PM POSHAN Scheme is implemented in partnership with the State Governments and UT Administrations. The overall responsibility for providing hot and nutritious meals to all children studying in Bal Vatika (just before class 1) and classes I to VIII of Government and Government aided schools lies with the State Governments and UT Administrations.
The Central Government provides 100% assistance for cost of foodgrains, transportation cost and cost of Management Monitoring & Evaluation (MME). As mandated under the Scheme, foodgrains are provided by Food Corporation of India (FCI). The allocation of foodgrains, as approved by the Programme Approval Board (PAB)- PM POSHAN are made to the State Nodal Department and the FCI. The foodgrains are allocated bi-annually by the Department of School.
Education and Literacy with the concurrence of the Department of Food and Public Distribution. The State-wise allocation of foodgrains during the last three years under PM Poshan Scheme is at Annexure-I. The Government of Uttar Pradesh has reported the district-wise number of children and foodgrains distributed under the scheme during the last three years is at Annexure-II.
It is the responsibility of the FCI to ensure continuous availability of adequate foodgrains in its Depots (and in Principal Distribution Centres in the case of North East Region). It allows lifting of foodgrains for any month/quarter upto one month in advance so that the supply chain of foodgrains remains uninterrupted. FCI issues foodgrains of best available quality, which in any case is at least of Fair Average Quality (FAQ). FCI has also appointed a Nodal Officer for each State to take care of various problems in supply of foodgrains under the Scheme. The District Collector/CEO of Zila Panchayat also ensures that foodgrains of at least FAQ are issued by FCI after joint inspection by a team consisting of FCI and the nominee of the Collector and/or Chief Executive Officer, District Panchayat, and confirmation by them that the grain conforms to at least FAQ norms. FCI keeps samples of such foodgrains supplied by it for future verification and analysis which is available in case of any complaints regarding the quality of foodgrains supplied.
The scheme also provides elaborate monitoring mechanism i.e. Empowered Committee under the Chairpersonship of Hon’ble Union Education Minister, Programme Approval Board (PAB) under the Chairpersonship of Secretary (DoSE&L), State Steering-cum-Monitoring Committee under the Chairpersonship of Chief Secretary, District level Steering-cum- Monitoring Committee under the Chairpersonship of District Collector. The PM Poshan Guidelines provides a District Level Committee under the Chairmanship of Senior Most Member of Parliament (MP) of the district to monitor the scheme on quarterly basis.
The States and UTs have developed dedicated mechanisms for public grievance redressal, which are widely publicized and made easily accessible (like toll free call facility etc.). The nutritional norms prescribed under the Scheme are displayed at prominent places visible to the common public. Further, the following information are also displayed on weekly/ monthly basis:
Weekly menu and its ingredients Quantity of food grains received and utilized Other ingredients purchased, utilized Number of children provided meals. Roster of Community Members involved in the programme.

enrichment.summary: In a Lok Sabha reply dated 10 August 2026, the Ministry of Education detailed the foodgrain allocation mechanism under the PM POSHAN scheme, under which the Centre bears 100% of foodgrain cost, transportation cost and Management, Monitoring & Evaluation (MME) expenses while states implement the scheme. Annexure data shows total foodgrain allocation across states/UTs declining from about 26.82 lakh MT in 2023-24 to about 24.15 lakh MT in 2025-26. District-wise data for Uttar Pradesh was also furnished, showing the number of children covered and quantity of foodgrains distributed across 75 districts over the last three years.
enrichment.context:
PM POSHAN (Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman), formerly the Mid-Day Meal Scheme, is a centrally sponsored scheme providing hot cooked meals to children in Bal Vatika and Classes I-VIII in government and government-aided schools, aimed at improving nutritional levels and school enrolment/retention. Since education falls under the Concurrent List, implementation responsibility rests with states/UTs while the Centre funds foodgrain costs, transportation and MME support, with the Food Corporation of India (FCI) supplying foodgrains of at least Fair Average Quality (FAQ). The scheme has a multi-tier monitoring structure—from the Empowered Committee chaired by the Union Education Minister down to District Level Committees chaired by the senior-most MP—reflecting the cooperative federalism model used for large welfare schemes.

The declining trend in total foodgrain allocation over three years (2023-24 to 2025-26) is significant for tracking enrolment trends, school nutrition coverage, and possible implications for child malnutrition indicators, especially as India continues to grapple with stunting and wasting concerns highlighted in reports like the National Family Health Survey (NFHS). Such parliamentary replies are also useful for aspirants to understand how centrally sponsored schemes function administratively, the quality-control mechanisms for foodgrain distribution, and the grievance redressal architecture mandated for welfare delivery.

prelims_questions.question:
Under the PM POSHAN Scheme, which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. The Central Government bears 100% of the cost of foodgrains, transportation, and Management, Monitoring & Evaluation (MME).
2. Foodgrains under the scheme are supplied by the Food Corporation of India.
3. Education, and hence implementation of PM POSHAN, is a subject exclusively under the Union List.
Select the correct answer using the code below:
prelims_questions.explanation: The release states the Centre provides 100% assistance for foodgrain cost, transportation, and MME, and that FCI supplies the foodgrains. However, education is part of the Concurrent List, not the Union List, making statement 3 incorrect.

prelims_questions.question: Which authority is responsible for approving the bi-annual allocation of foodgrains to States/UTs under the PM POSHAN Scheme?
options: Empowered Committee under the Union Education Minister
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, foodgrain allocation is approved by the Programme Approval Board (PAB)-PM POSHAN and made to the State Nodal Department and FCI with concurrence of the Department of Food and Public Distribution.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the institutional mechanism for implementation and monitoring of the PM POSHAN Scheme in India. Examine the challenges of cooperative federalism in delivering centrally sponsored nutrition schemes.

Nutritional support schemes like PM POSHAN are critical instruments in addressing child malnutrition in India. Critically evaluate the effectiveness of such schemes and suggest measures to improve last-mile delivery and quality assurance of foodgrains.
